text.p: Nicaraguan police on Friday arrested the man accused of leading the spectacular 1993 assault and hostage-taking of the Nicaraguan embassy in Costa Rica, a police spokesman said.
Jose Manuel Urbina Lara was arrested in Managua's international airport as he arrived on a flight from Panama, police spokesman Capt. Justo Zamora told Reuters.
It was not immediately clear why he had returned to the country.

Urbina Lara had led the Commando Yolaina, an armed band linked to Nicaragua's former Contra rebels, who in March 1993 took 13 hostages, including the Nicaraguan ambassador Alfonso Robelo, at the Nicaraguan embassy in Costa Rica and held them for 13 days before releasing them.
They had demanded a ransom and that the Nicaraguan government fulfil the terms of the 1990 peace agreement that ended Nicaragua's civil war.
Urbina Lara escaped with the $250,000 ransom and Nicaraguan police say he fled to the Dominican Republic.
Zamora said Urbina Lara will be brought before a Nicaragua court.
